script:
# A forced failure: `mock` makes the next call to items.fetch throw, and the screen reports the error code.
# The rows that were already loaded stay, the way a real list keeps its contents when a refresh fails.
expect screen=items items=3 error=none
mock items.fetch network
refresh
expect error=network items=3 loading=false call=items.fetch
# `retry` is gated on there being an error, so it is offered only now; before the failure the runner refuses it
# with `retry is disabled here (error=none)`. The fault is one-shot, so this load succeeds.
retry
expect error=none items=3 call=items.fetch

script:
# The cooldown: a second save while the countdown is running is refused with error=cooldown, and the countdown
# keeps going. `pending=1` is that countdown waiting on the clock; `advance` is what releases it.
# app-test: skip it checks the countdown's exact values, which in the app also tick in real time
open 2
expect screen=items/2 cooldown=0 error=none
save
expect saved=true cooldown=3 pending=1 error=none
save
expect error=cooldown saved=true cooldown=3 pending=1
advance 1s
expect cooldown=2 pending=1 error=cooldown
advance 2s
expect cooldown=0 pending=0 error=none
# Saving is allowed again.
save
expect saved=true cooldown=3 pending=1 error=none
